intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise
experiences.description: Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Enjoy breathtaking Hawaiian sunsets, spot sea turtles and dolphins, and experience the ocean breeze while avoiding peak daytime heat. Many operators include snacks and drinks.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show
experiences.description: Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This indoor and covered-venue experience showcases the traditions, music, and dance of six Pacific Island cultures, making it ideal for families and perfectly timed to avoid daytime heat.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking
experiences.description: Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours before temperatures peak. Paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands, spot sea turtles, and enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters. Equipment and safety gear are included in the rental.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Honolulu International Airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Collect luggage, pick up a TheBus pass (affordable public transit), and head to your accommodation to check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short trip to Waikiki Beach — one of Hawaii's most iconic and free beaches. Enjoy the warm sand, gentle waves, and stunning views of Diamond Head. Great for families with kids of all ages. Rent a boogie board from a local vendor for around $10.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's main strip. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free nightly shows). Enjoy the festive atmosphere without spending a dime.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a plate lunch from a local food truck near Waikiki — try Spam musubi or a chicken katsu plate for under $12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Marugame Udon in Waikiki — hearty udon noodle bowls starting at $6–$9, perfect for families on a budget.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts after 11:20 AM arrival. Purchase a 7-day TheBus pass ($35/adult, $17.50/child) for unlimited rides — the most budget-friendly way to get around Oahu.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument. Take TheBus to the trailhead and hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater. Entry is $5/person. The panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific Ocean are breathtaking and well worth the effort for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kapiolani Park, a large free public park at the base of Diamond Head. Enjoy a picnic lunch on the grass, let the kids run around, and explore the free Honolulu Zoo entrance area. The park often has free weekend events and local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall. Browse local shops, enjoy free entertainment, and grab an affordable dinner at the food court.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh fruit and pastries from the ABC Store or a local convenience store near your hotel — budget around $5–$8 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a nearby grocery store (Foodland or Times Supermarket) — sandwiches, chips, and drinks for the whole family under $20 total.
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Food Court — wide variety of local Hawaiian, Japanese, and American options ranging from $8–$14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Diamond Head hike. Bring sunscreen, water, and hats. August weather averages around 16.8°C (62°F) highs — light layers recommended for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Oahu's best snorkeling spots. Entry is $25/adult (children 12 and under free). Arrive early as entry is limited. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among colorful fish and coral reefs in a protected bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapuu Point Lookout. The easy 2-mile round-trip paved trail offers stunning coastal views and is free. Look for humpback whales (seasonal) and enjoy the dramatic cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a relaxing evening on the beach watching the sunset. The sky over the Pacific at dusk is spectacular and completely free.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Liliha Bakery — famous for their coco puffs and pancakes, budget around $10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and sandwiches from a grocery store to enjoy at Hanauma Bay or Makapuu — saves money and keeps energy up for activities.
meals.dinner: Rainbow Drive-In — a beloved local institution serving plate lunches and burgers. Meals from $9–$13. Very family-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations ($1 booking fee). Snorkel gear rental is available on-site for about $12. No touching the coral — it's a protected marine sanctuary.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial and Pearl Harbor Historic Sites. The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free (reserve online in advance). The visitor center and museum are also free. A deeply moving and educational experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free exhibits at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center, including the Road to War exhibit and the Remembrance Circle. If budget allows, add the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum ($27/adult, $15/child) for an interactive family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Chinatown in downtown Honolulu for a cultural evening stroll. Browse local art galleries (many open late on Fridays for First Friday events), street art, and vibrant local culture.

meals.breakfast: Zippy's Restaurant — a Hawaii chain staple. Try their saimin or breakfast plate for $8–$12. Great local flavor.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center café or pack your own lunch to eat at the picnic areas near the memorial.
meals.dinner: Chinatown's Little Village Noodle House — authentic Chinese-Hawaiian cuisine with generous portions. Dishes from $10–$16, perfect for sharing as a family.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is very popular — book the USS Arizona Memorial tour weeks in advance online (free but limited spots). Bags larger than 1 gallon are not permitted inside the memorial area.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus to the North Shore — about a 1.5-hour scenic ride. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park, one of Oahu's most beautiful beaches. In summer, the water is calm and perfect for swimming and snorkeling. The beach is free and stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Kamehameha Highway to Haleiwa Town — the charming surf town of the North Shore. Browse local boutiques, surf shops, and art galleries. Stop at the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice for a classic Hawaiian treat ($4–$6).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Sunset Beach — one of the most iconic surf spots in the world. In summer, the waves are gentle and the beach is peaceful. Return to Honolulu via TheBus.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before heading out — try a local plate from 7-Eleven Hawaii (surprisingly good local options like musubi for $2–$4).
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — world-famous garlic shrimp plates for $15. A North Shore institution and worth every penny.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries at a Haleiwa store or grab a quick meal at a local food truck before heading back. Budget $10–$15.

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore bus ride is long but scenic and free with your bus pass. Bring a full water bottle, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the evening return trip. August is the best time for calm North Shore waters.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Admission is $27/adult and $19/child. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium, and fascinating exhibits on Polynesian culture. Educational and engaging for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nuuanu Pali Lookout — a dramatic cliffside viewpoint with sweeping views of the Koolau Mountains and windward Oahu. Entry is $7 per car (free if arriving by bus). The views are absolutely stunning and the site has deep historical significance.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Ala Moana Beach Park — a local favorite with calm, protected waters perfect for families. Watch locals play volleyball, fish, and enjoy the park. Free and beautiful at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at your accommodation or grab items from a nearby grocery store — yogurt, fruit, and granola bars for $5–$8 total.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Bishop Museum café or pack your own. Alternatively, grab plate lunches from a nearby food truck for $10–$13.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood — a tiny, beloved local spot near Ala Moana serving fresh poke bowls for $12–$16. One of the best poke in Honolulu.

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is excellent for families with children — the Science Adventure Center has hands-on exhibits kids love. Check for any free or discounted admission days.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Manoa Falls Trail — a lush, easy 1.6-mile round-trip hike through a tropical rainforest leading to a beautiful 150-foot waterfall. Parking is $5 or take TheBus. Free trail entry. Wear water-resistant shoes as the trail can be muddy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lyon Arboretum near the trailhead — a free botanical garden with over 5,000 tropical plant species. A peaceful and educational afternoon for the whole family among exotic flowers and towering trees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a final evening beach walk. Enjoy the free Kuhio Beach Torch Lighting and Hula Show at 6:30 PM (Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday) — a wonderful cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Waiola Shave Ice & Bakery — try their fresh malasadas (Portuguese donuts) for $2–$3 each, a Hawaiian breakfast staple.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a grocery store to enjoy at the arboretum or after the hike. Budget $15–$20 for the family.
meals.dinner: Side Street Inn on Hopaka — a local favorite with generous portions of local-style comfort food. Dishes $12–$18. Great for families.

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls trail is beautiful but can be slippery after rain (176mm average rainfall in August). Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light rain jacket. The trail is suitable for older children but may be challenging for toddlers.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of historic downtown Honolulu. Visit Iolani Palace (exterior free, interior tours $27/adult, $7/child) — the only royal palace on US soil. Walk to the King Kamehameha Statue and the Hawaii State Capitol, all within easy walking distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kailua Beach on the windward side of Oahu — consistently rated one of America's best beaches. The calm, turquoise waters and white sand are perfect for families. Take TheBus (about 1 hour) or rent a car for the day. Beach access is free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kailua Town — a charming, laid-back community with local boutiques, galleries, and restaurants. Browse the shops and enjoy the relaxed local vibe before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Café Julia in downtown Honolulu — a charming café with affordable breakfast options from $8–$14 in a historic building.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — a beloved local deli with fresh sandwiches, salads, and snacks. Budget $10–$15 per person.
meals.dinner: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their red velvet pancakes and local comfort food. Dinner options from $12–$18.

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is worth the trip across the island. The windward side tends to be slightly cooler and greener. Kayak rentals are available near the beach for $25–$40/hour if the family wants an extra adventure.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Sea Life Park Hawaii on the southeastern coast — a family-friendly marine park with dolphin shows, sea turtle exhibits, penguin encounters, and a Hawaiian reef tank. Admission is $40/adult and $20/child. Book online for discounts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Makapuu Beach Park on the way back — a beautiful beach popular with bodyboarders. The waves can be strong, so supervise children carefully. The beach is free and the scenery is dramatic with black lava cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening at Waikiki Beach for a final sunset swim. Pick up some local souvenirs from the ABC Stores (affordable and convenient) or the International Market Place.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at your accommodation or pick up items from a grocery store — fruit, yogurt, and juice for $5–$8 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from a grocery store to enjoy at Sea Life Park's picnic areas — saves money compared to park food prices.
meals.dinner: Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki — a beloved local breakfast-all-day spot. Pancakes, waffles, and local dishes from $10–$16. Great for families.

day_by_day.notes: Sea Life Park offers family packages that can reduce per-person costs. Check their website for online discount codes before purchasing tickets. The park is a highlight for children and offers unique Hawaiian marine life education.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — take one last walk along Waikiki Beach at sunrise. Collect shells, take photos, and soak in the beauty of the Pacific. Visit the Honolulu Farmers Market at KCC (Kapiolani Community College) if it falls on a Saturday — fresh local produce, food vendors, and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the International Market Place or Ala Moana Center. Pick up local treats like macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian sea salt — great affordable gifts. Head to the airport with plenty of time for your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Honolulu International Airport. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with beautiful beaches, rich culture, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: One final breakfast at a local spot — try Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen for their famous macadamia nut pancakes ($12–$15). A perfect farewell meal.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable lunch at the airport or pick up plate lunches from a nearby food truck before heading to check-in.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner before departure — most Honolulu Airport restaurants offer local options from $12–$20.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Return your TheBus pass if applicable. Pack any fresh fruit or local food items carefully — agricultural restrictions apply when leaving Hawaii. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 — Flight lands, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Check-in and freshen up after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby family-friendly restaurant for a relaxed welcome dinner. Explore the Buena Park entertainment strip along Beach Boulevard for a casual evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light bite at the airport before or after landing — airport café or grab-and-go snacks (~$10–15/person)
meals.lunch: In-N-Out Burger or Panda Express near the hotel for a quick, affordable mid-day meal (~$10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Sizzler or Denny's near Buena Park for a relaxed family dinner (~$15–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, Day 1 is intentionally light. Focus on rest and recovery. Confirm any pre-booked Hawaii activity reservations and review the upcoming itinerary. Note: The hotel is in Buena Park, CA — this itinerary assumes the Hawaii portion begins Day 2 with a connecting or onward flight, or that Days 1–2 are a California layover before the Hawaii leg begins.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Buena Park — head to LAX or John Wayne Airport for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Arrive in Honolulu mid-morning and transfer to your Oahu accommodation. Check in and change into beach attire.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head straight to Waikiki Beach for your first taste of Hawaii. Rent beach chairs and umbrellas (~$20/set), swim in the calm turquoise waters, and let the kids build sandcastles. Walk the famous Kalakaua Avenue and browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Watch the stunning Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean with the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Airport breakfast at LAX — grab pastries and coffee at a café (~$12–18/person)
meals.lunch: Eggs 'n Things on Waikiki — iconic Hawaiian breakfast-all-day spot, great for families (~$15–20/person)
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — classic beachfront restaurant with Hawaiian-inspired dishes and a lively atmosphere (~$25–40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sunset Catamaran Cruise in advance as spots fill quickly, especially for families. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, as Hawaii law requires it. Average high is around 17°C so evenings on the water may feel cool — bring a light jacket for the cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking — Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours. Paddle through crystal-clear waters and explore the scenic Mokulua Islands offshore. Perfect for all skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, relax on Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches. Build sandcastles, snorkel in the shallow reef areas, or simply enjoy the powdery white sand. Explore the charming Kailua town for local boutiques and ice cream.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu and visit the Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall — for some window shopping and a casual dinner at the food court or surrounding restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's at the Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — famous for their red velvet pancakes and local breakfast favorites (~$15–22/person)
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — grab fresh sandwiches, salads, and local snacks for a beach picnic (~$12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus in Ala Moana or Panda Express food court for a budget-friendly option (~$15–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: Kailua is about 30–40 minutes from Waikiki by car. Rent a car or book a rideshare for the day. Morning kayaking is ideal before the midday heat. Bring water shoes for the rocky entry points at Kailua Beach.

day_by_day.morning: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits — Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, Science Adventure Center, and planetarium shows. Great for curious kids and adults alike.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, drive to Punchbowl Crater (National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific) for a scenic and historically significant stop. Then head to Nuuanu Pali Lookout for breathtaking panoramic views of the Windward Coast — a must-see Oahu landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show — Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Enjoy traditional Polynesian food, fire knife dancing, and a spectacular theatrical performance.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery — a beloved local institution known for coco puffs and hearty breakfasts (~$12–18/person)
meals.lunch: Café on-site at the Bishop Museum — convenient and reasonably priced (~$12–16/person)
meals.dinner: Included in the Polynesian Cultural Center luau package — traditional Hawaiian buffet with kalua pig, poi, and island desserts (~$50–70/person, part of show package)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Polynesian Cultural Center show well in advance — it's one of Oahu's most popular evening experiences. The center is located in Laie, about 1 hour from Waikiki, so plan transportation accordingly. The luau dinner is typically included in the show ticket package.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument — hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit of the volcanic crater for stunning 360-degree views of Honolulu and the coastline. The hike takes about 1.5–2 hours and is suitable for older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for world-class snorkeling in a protected marine sanctuary. Watch the mandatory educational video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in the calm, shallow bay. Arrive early as entry is limited.
day_by_day.evening: Relax back in Waikiki with a sunset stroll along the beachfront. Visit the International Market Place for souvenir shopping and enjoy a casual dinner at one of the open-air restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Bogart's Café near Diamond Head — açaí bowls, smoothies, and light breakfast fare (~$12–18/person)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for Hanauma Bay — bring sandwiches and fruit from a nearby grocery store to save money (~$8–12/person)
meals.dinner: Yard House at International Market Place — wide menu with something for everyone, great for families (~$20–35/person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations ($25/adult, children under 12 free). The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Diamond Head parking fills up early — arrive before 8 AM or take TheBus. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and water for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu to Kahului, Maui (short 30-minute inter-island flight). Pick up a rental car and drive the scenic Road to Hana — stop at Twin Falls for a short waterfall hike, and enjoy the lush rainforest scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Road to Hana — visit Wai'anapanapa State Park with its dramatic black sand beach and sea caves. Walk the coastal trail and take in the rugged volcanic landscape. Book a timed entry reservation in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hana town for a relaxing evening. Explore the small town, visit Hasegawa General Store, and settle into your Maui accommodation for the night.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Kahului Airport or a nearby café before heading out (~$10–15/person)
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — try fresh banana bread from Aunty Sandy's, fruit stands, and local plate lunches (~$10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Hana Ranch Restaurant in Hana town — casual dining with local Hawaiian flavors (~$20–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is about 65 miles but takes 3–4 hours due to winding roads and stops. Start early. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations ($5/person parking fee). The road can be narrow — drive carefully and pull over to let locals pass.

day_by_day.morning: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, sharks, and coral reef ecosystems. Walk through the 750,000-gallon Open Ocean tank tunnel — a highlight for kids and adults. Located in Ma'alaea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ka'anapali Beach on Maui's west coast — one of the island's most beautiful stretches of sand. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on the beach. Walk the Ka'anapali Beachwalk boardwalk and explore the Whalers Village shopping center.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at sunset — a free and spectacular local tradition. Then enjoy dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Ka'anapali.

meals.breakfast: Café O'Lei at the Maui Ocean Center — convenient breakfast before the aquarium opens (~$12–18/person)
meals.lunch: Leoda's Kitchen and Pie Shop in Olowalu — famous for their savory pies and fresh local ingredients (~$15–20/person)
meals.dinner: Hula Grill Ka'anapali — open-air beachfront dining with fresh seafood and Hawaiian cuisine (~$25–40/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Maui Ocean Center opens at 9 AM — arrive early to beat crowds. Ka'anapali Beach is about 45 minutes from Ma'alaea. The Black Rock cliff diving ceremony typically happens at sunset — check the exact time with your hotel. Parking at Ka'anapali can be expensive; use the Whalers Village lot.

day_by_day.morning: Drive up to Haleakalā National Park for a morning visit to the summit (10,023 feet). Explore the otherworldly volcanic crater landscape, walk the Pā Ka'oao (White Hill) trail, and enjoy the dramatic above-the-clouds scenery. Bring warm layers — it's significantly colder at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakalā and head to Makena Beach (Big Beach) — one of Maui's largest and most beautiful beaches. Bodysurf the waves, explore Little Beach around the rocky point, and soak up the afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Maui accommodation and enjoy a relaxed evening in Kihei or Wailea. Browse the Azeka Shopping Center or enjoy a sunset dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from a grocery store the night before — eat at the Haleakalā summit for a memorable experience (~$8–12/person)
meals.lunch: Coconut's Fish Café in Kihei — beloved local spot for fresh fish tacos and plate lunches (~$12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Monkeypod Kitchen in Wailea — farm-to-table menu with craft cocktails and a lively family-friendly atmosphere (~$25–40/person)

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā National Park requires advance timed entry reservations for sunrise visits ($35/vehicle). For a morning visit (not sunrise), reservations are still recommended. Temperatures at the summit can be near freezing — bring jackets, hats, and layers for the whole family. Makena Beach has strong shore break; supervise children closely.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning snorkel boat tour to Molokini Crater — a partially submerged volcanic crater and marine sanctuary offering some of Hawaii's best snorkeling with 150-foot visibility. Most tours depart from Ma'alaea Harbor at 7–8 AM and return by noon.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat tour, visit the charming historic town of Lahaina. Walk Front Street, explore the Baldwin Home Museum, and see the famous 150-year-old Banyan Tree in Banyan Tree Park. Browse local art galleries and boutique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your final Maui evening with a traditional Hawaiian luau experience — book the Old Lahaina Luau for an authentic, intimate cultural experience with traditional food, hula dancing, and storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks on the boat — most Molokini tours provide continental breakfast or snacks on board (~included in tour)
meals.lunch: Aloha Mixed Plate in Lahaina — casual beachfront spot with affordable Hawaiian plate lunches (~$12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — traditional Hawaiian buffet included in the luau package (~$50–80/person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini snorkel tour and Old Lahaina Luau well in advance — both are extremely popular and sell out weeks ahead. The Old Lahaina Luau is considered one of the most authentic luau experiences in Hawaii. Bring motion sickness medication if needed for the boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Maui — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take one last walk on your favorite Maui beach. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at local stores or the Maui Swap Meet (open Saturday mornings) for affordable local crafts and produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your Maui accommodation and drive to Kahului Airport. Return the rental car and check in for your flight back to the mainland. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Fly back to the mainland — arrive back in California and transfer to the SureStay Hotel in Buena Park if needed, or continue to your final destination.

meals.breakfast: Café Mambo or Maui Coffee Roasters in Kahului — local coffee shop with fresh pastries and breakfast bowls (~$12–18/person)
meals.lunch: Zippy's or L&L Hawaiian Barbecue at the airport or nearby — classic Hawaiian comfort food for a final island meal (~$12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal on the return journey (~$15–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for car return, shuttle, and airport check-in at Kahului Airport. Pick up any last-minute gifts at the airport duty-free or ABC Stores. Consider buying local Maui coffee, macadamia nuts, and Hawaiian sea salt as affordable, authentic souvenirs. Mahalo for a wonderful Hawaii trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise
experiences.description: Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Enjoy breathtaking Hawaiian sunsets, spot sea turtles and dolphins, and experience the ocean breeze while avoiding peak daytime heat. Many operators include snacks and drinks.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show
experiences.description: Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This indoor and covered-venue experience showcases the traditions, music, and dance of six Pacific Island cultures, making it ideal for families and perfectly timed to avoid daytime heat.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking
experiences.description: Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours before temperatures peak. Paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands, spot sea turtles, and enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters. Equipment and safety gear are included in the rental.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to your luxury accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your hotel and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll along the nearest beach to acclimate to the island atmosphere. Enjoy the warm Hawaiian sun and turquoise waters at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Watch the stunning Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean while enjoying light refreshments on board.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant offering fresh Hawaiian seafood and island-inspired cuisine with stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion dining experience with premium sushi and signature black cod dishes

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule light to allow for jet lag recovery and settling in. Confirm catamaran cruise booking in advance as sunset slots fill up quickly in August.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking — Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours. Paddle through crystal-clear waters and explore the scenic coastline, with expert guides ensuring a safe and memorable experience for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Kailua Beach — one of Hawaii's most pristine white-sand beaches. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, snorkel in the calm turquoise waters, and enjoy the natural beauty of the windward coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area for a relaxed evening. Explore the upscale shops at Royal Hawaiian Center and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant at the Ilima Hotel — famous for their fluffy pancakes and local Hawaiian breakfast favorites
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Café & Deli in Kailua — beloved local spot with gourmet sandwiches, fresh salads, and artisan coffee
meals.dinner: The Pig and the Lady — award-winning Honolulu restaurant blending Vietnamese and Hawaiian flavors with locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is approximately 30–40 minutes from central Honolulu. Book kayaking tour in advance. August mornings are ideal for kayaking before afternoon trade winds pick up.

day_by_day.morning: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits — Visit Hawaii's largest and most prestigious museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Polynesian culture. Explore the iconic Hawaiian Hall, planetarium shows, and hands-on science exhibits perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Iolani Palace — the only royal palace on American soil — for a guided tour. Explore the beautifully restored rooms and learn about Hawaii's royal history. Afterward, stroll through the Capitol District and browse the Honolulu Farmers Market.
day_by_day.evening: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show — Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Enjoy a premium luau dinner followed by a breathtaking theatrical performance celebrating Polynesian heritage.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things — iconic Honolulu breakfast spot famous for their crepes, waffles, and fresh tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Livestock Tavern — Honolulu's celebrated farm-to-table restaurant with artisan burgers and locally sourced seasonal dishes
meals.dinner: Included in the Polynesian Cultural Center luau package — a lavish buffet featuring traditional Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is located on the North Shore (approximately 1 hour from Honolulu). Book the Ambassador VIP package for the best experience including reserved front-row seating and private dining. The evening show typically runs until 9:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Fly to Maui — Take an early inter-island flight (approximately 30 minutes). Check in to your luxury Maui resort. Freshen up and head to Ka'anapali Beach, consistently ranked among the world's best beaches, for a morning swim and snorkel session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, sharks, and vibrant coral reef ecosystems. The open-ocean tunnel and touch pools are especially engaging for families. Spend 2–3 hours exploring all exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Ka'anapali Beach — Watch the legendary Cliff Diver ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) as a local diver leaps from the lava rock at sunset, a nightly Maui tradition. Enjoy cocktails at a beachfront bar.

meals.breakfast: In-room dining at your Honolulu hotel before departure — fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman in Ka'anapali — farm-to-table Maui cuisine with handcrafted cocktails and stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill — Maui's most celebrated fine dining restaurant with innovative American cuisine and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines for the most reliable service. Confirm Maui luxury resort reservation (recommend Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Montage Kapalua Bay). Maui Ocean Center is best visited in the afternoon to avoid morning crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana Sunrise Drive — Embark on the iconic Road to Hana, one of the world's most scenic coastal drives. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the bamboo forest, and marvel at the dramatic sea cliffs. Hire a private driver or rent a premium SUV for maximum comfort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana — Visit the stunning black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park, explore the sacred Pools of 'Ohe'o (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakalā National Park, and hike through lush rainforest trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Maui resort. Unwind with a luxury spa treatment at the resort spa — choose from traditional Hawaiian lomilomi massage or a couple's oceanfront treatment.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your resort before departure — fresh açaí bowls, tropical fruit platters, and Maui-grown coffee
meals.lunch: Café Romantica in Hana — charming roadside café with fresh sandwiches, smoothies, and local snacks perfect for a Road to Hana pit stop
meals.dinner: Spago by Wolfgang Puck at Four Seasons Maui — celebrity chef dining with Pacific Rim cuisine and panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles with over 600 curves and 59 bridges — allow a full day. Start early (before 7 AM) to beat traffic. Bring sunscreen, water, and light rain gear as August can bring brief tropical showers. Reserve spa treatments in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakalā Sunrise Experience — Wake before dawn for the breathtaking sunrise above the clouds at Haleakalā Crater (summit at 10,023 feet). This is one of Hawaii's most iconic and spiritual experiences. Book a guided sunrise tour for the most enriching experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wailea Beach Afternoon — Return to the resort and spend a relaxing afternoon at the pristine Wailea Beach. Enjoy premium beach service, paddleboarding, or a private snorkeling excursion to explore Maui's vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Dinner Cruise from Ma'alaea Harbor — Board a luxury catamaran for a premium sunset dinner cruise along Maui's coastline. Enjoy gourmet canapés, open bar, and live Hawaiian music while watching the sun dip below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks and hot beverages provided during the Haleakalā sunrise tour
meals.lunch: Ferraro's Bar e Ristorante at Four Seasons Maui — authentic Italian cuisine with fresh pasta and wood-fired dishes overlooking the ocean
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner served on board the sunset cruise — fresh seafood, premium meats, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā sunrise requires a timed entry reservation through the National Park Service — book months in advance as permits sell out quickly. Temperatures at the summit can drop to near freezing even in August — bring warm layers. The drive to the summit takes approximately 1.5 hours from Wailea.

day_by_day.morning: Molokini Crater Snorkeling Expedition — Board a premium catamaran for an exclusive snorkeling tour to Molokini Crater, a partially submerged volcanic caldera teeming with over 250 species of tropical fish and crystal-clear visibility up to 150 feet. Perfect for families of all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly to the Big Island of Hawaii — Take an inter-island flight to Kona or Hilo. Check in to your luxury Big Island resort. Visit the stunning Hapuna Beach, one of Hawaii's largest and most beautiful white-sand beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Kailua-Kona town. Browse the oceanfront Ali'i Drive, visit the historic Hulihe'e Palace, and enjoy the vibrant sunset atmosphere along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Maui resort — fresh tropical fruit, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and snacks provided on the Molokini snorkeling catamaran
meals.dinner: Brown's Beach House at Fairmont Orchid — Big Island's premier oceanfront fine dining with locally sourced Hawaiian cuisine and live music

day_by_day.notes: Molokini tours depart early from Ma'alaea Harbor — confirm departure time with tour operator. Book the premium private charter option for a more exclusive experience. Recommend staying at Fairmont Orchid or Four Seasons Resort Hualalai on the Big Island.

day_by_day.morning: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — Explore one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Visit the Kilauea Visitor Center, walk the Crater Rim Trail, peer into the glowing Halema'uma'u Crater, and explore the otherworldly Thurston Lava Tube. A truly unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — Drive the Chain of Craters Road to the coast, passing ancient lava flows and dramatic sea arches. Visit the Pu'u Loa Petroglyphs, one of Hawaii's largest ancient petroglyph fields.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kona area. Enjoy a relaxing evening at your resort with a private beachside bonfire experience (available at select luxury resorts) or a stargazing session — the Big Island has some of the world's clearest night skies.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your resort before the drive to Volcanoes National Park (approximately 1.5 hours from Kona)
meals.lunch: Café Ono at Volcano House Hotel — charming historic lodge restaurant inside the national park with panoramic crater views
meals.dinner: Merriman's Waimea — Big Island's iconic farm-to-table restaurant founded by Peter Merriman, pioneer of Hawaii Regional Cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park requires a $35 vehicle entry fee (valid for 7 days). Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current volcanic activity updates before visiting. The drive from Kona to the park is approximately 1.5–2 hours — consider an early start.

day_by_day.morning: Manta Ray Night Snorkeling Preparation and Morning Beach Day — Spend a relaxing morning at the resort beach. Enjoy premium water sports including stand-up paddleboarding, outrigger canoe paddling, or a private surf lesson with a professional instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Waipio Valley Lookout and Cultural Tour — Visit the dramatic Waipio Valley, the 'Valley of the Kings,' with its towering 2,000-foot cliffs, black sand beach, and lush taro fields. Take a guided cultural tour to learn about the valley's deep significance in Hawaiian history and mythology.
day_by_day.evening: Manta Ray Night Snorkeling — Experience one of Hawaii's most magical wildlife encounters. Snorkel or dive with giant Pacific manta rays (with wingspans up to 14 feet) as they gracefully feed on plankton illuminated by underwater lights. A truly bucket-list family experience.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at your resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh açaí bowls, loco moco, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Bamboo Restaurant in Hawi — beloved North Kohala restaurant with Pacific Rim cuisine in a charming plantation-era building
meals.dinner: CanoeHouse at Mauna Lani — award-winning oceanfront restaurant with innovative Hawaiian cuisine and an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray snorkeling tours depart from Keauhou Bay or Garden Eel Cove in the evening — book with a reputable operator such as Jack's Diving Locker or Manta Ray Advocates. Manta ray sightings are not guaranteed but occur on approximately 90% of tours. Life jackets available for non-swimmers.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning at Hapuna Beach — Spend your last morning at the stunning Hapuna Beach, consistently ranked among the world's top beaches. Enjoy a final swim, collect shells, and soak in the breathtaking views of the Kohala Coast one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Resort Spa Farewell Treatment — Indulge in a signature Hawaiian spa experience at your resort. Choose from a traditional lomilomi massage, volcanic stone therapy, or a couples' oceanfront treatment. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kona International Airport — Transfer to the airport for your return flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with world-class beaches, cultural experiences, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at your resort — full Hawaiian breakfast spread with fresh tropical fruits, macadamia nut pancakes, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Lava Lava Beach Club — casual yet upscale beachfront dining with fresh fish tacos, poke bowls, and tropical cocktails with your feet in the sand
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — pick up local treats and macadamia nut chocolates from Kona International Airport shops as souvenirs

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security at Kona International Airport. Consider shipping any large souvenir purchases home to avoid baggage fees. Purchase fresh Kona coffee, Hawaiian sea salt, and local honey as premium gifts to bring home.
